name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.blocker_text: 10 continuous years of legal residence, plus passing a citizenship test.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 10 continuous years' legal residence and pass the citizenship test.

requirement_groups.name: Expedited procedure (Spain, Portugal, Italy, Latin American/Caribbean nationals)

requirements.blocker_text: Nationals of Spain, Portugal, Italy, or any Latin American or Caribbean country qualify after only 5 continuous years of legal residence -- half the standard track. This is a genuine, real reduction tied to national origin, not a general rule.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 continuous years' legal residence as a qualifying national, and pass the citizenship test.

evidence_required.document: Proof of continuous legal residence (5 or 10 years depending on nationality)
Passing result on the citizenship test

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: continuous legal residence for the qualifying period

sources.title: Wikipedia -- 10-year general naturalization track, the 5-year expedited track for Spanish/Portuguese/Italian/Latin American/Caribbean nationals, the citizenship test, and Article 34's dual-nationality allowance

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Venezuela). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-4 sourcing only; Venezuela's own Ley de Nacionalidad y Ciudadania text and Constitution Article 34 were not independently fetched from a government source in this build (a mppre.gob.ve page on naturalization returned a 404 error). GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE FINDING: the 5-year Ibero-American/Latin American/Caribbean expedited track is a real, historically-rooted regional preference (reflecting Venezuela's long-standing 'hermano latinoamericano' framing), structurally similar in shape to Kuwait's Arab-nationality naturalization preference and Senegal's ECOWAS-adjacent treatment built elsewhere in this dataset, though here applied as a residency-length reduction rather than a full discretionary bypass. dual_citizenship_allowed set true per Article 34's stated allowance -- if accurate, this is a genuine positive finding distinguishing Venezuela from most naturalization-renunciation regimes built in this dataset (e.g. Kuwait, Uzbekistan, DR Congo), though the constitutional citation itself should be verified directly against Venezuela's government gazette in a follow-up given the tier-4-only sourcing here. GOVERNANCE-TRANSITION CAVEAT: as with every route in this Venezuela build, whether and how naturalization decisions are currently being processed under the Rodriguez-led acting government (see ve_visitor_visa.json's notes) was not confirmed.
